simple.meaning: מַתָּן (mattân) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a present.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Genesis, Numbers, Proverbs, beginning at Genesis 34:12. Its contexts include family line, offering, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַתָּן (H4976).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַתָּן (mattân) / H4976 is traced through Genesis 34:12, Numbers 18:11, Proverbs 18:16, Proverbs 19:6 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”

majorEvents.label: Offering
majorEvents.evidenceText: “This is yours, too: the wave offering of their gift, even all the wave offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a portion forever. Everyone who is clean in your house shall eat of it.

definitions.full: H4976. mattan I. מַתָּן noun masculine Prov 18:16 collective gift(s) ; — absolute ׳מ Gen 34:12 2 t.; construct id. Prov 18:16 (see Baer on the passage Ges § 92g Kö ii 1, 98 ); suffix מַתָּנָם Num 18:11 ; — marriage- gifts Gen 34:12 (J; + מֹהַר ); offerings Num 18:11 (P; מ ׳תְּרוּמַת ); elsewhere Generally, gifts, presents , Prov 18:16 ; 21:14 (|| שֹׁחַד ); מַתָּן אִישׁ 19:6 = a giver of gifts .
